summary: Removed .refine(mutuallyExclusivePaths, { message: MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG }) from all 18 schema definitions across 7 tool files using perl multi-line replacement. Cleaned up all unused imports of mutuallyExclusivePaths and MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG from all 7 tool files. InitializeProjectSchema (field-level .refine() on plan_file) is untouched. TypeScript compiles clean (exit 0). All 1014 tests pass across 33 test files. No regressions introduced.

comments.note: The mutuallyExclusivePaths function and MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG constant remain exported from path-validator.ts and are covered by tests, but are no longer used by any production tool file. They are effectively dead code outside of tests. Future consideration (not in scope for this WP): if the Zod schema-level refinement approach is never re-adopted, these exports could be marked as test-only or removed in a future cleanup. Currently retained for backward compatibility per the plan.

summary: All 5 acceptance criteria verified and confirmed. TypeScript compiles without errors (exit 0). All 1014 tests pass across 33 test files. No regressions introduced. Static grep confirms zero schema-level .refine() calls remain in any tool file. The only .refine() is the preserved field-level plan_file refinement inside InitializeProjectSchema. Both mutuallyExclusivePaths and MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG are absent from all 7 tool files. Implementation is clean and correct.

Runtime import-based schema type checks return undefined (not ZodEffects), which is expected. Authoritative verification was done via: (1) static grep showing zero schema-level .refine() calls, (2) tsc --noEmit exiting 0, (3) full test suite passing 1014/1014.

Edge case verified: InitializeProjectSchema's plan_file field-level .refine() at project-lifecycle.ts:377 is intact and untouched, correctly producing a ZodString with refinement inside a ZodObject rather than a ZodEffects-wrapped schema.

summary: Code review passed. The 18 `.refine()` removals across 7 tool files are surgically clean — no dangling syntax, no orphaned imports, no split commas. Independently verified: (1) grep confirms zero schema-level `.refine()` calls remain in tool files; (2) `tsc --noEmit` exits 0; (3) `InitializeProjectSchema` plan_file `.refine()` at project-lifecycle.ts:377 is intact. The runtime guard (`resolveProjectPath` throws `MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG` at path-validator.ts:70) correctly preserves the mutual-exclusivity contract at the function boundary. Dead exports (`mutuallyExclusivePaths`, `MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG`) remain in path-validator.ts as intended — covered by tests and retained for backward compatibility per WP scope. One non-blocking suggestion filed.

summary: Updated two manifest documents to reflect the architectural change from WP-001/WP-002: (1) api-surface.md — updated the resolveProjectPath() comment to remove stale 'defence in depth alongside any Zod .refine()' language (the calling schemas are now plain ZodObjects); updated the mutuallyExclusivePaths documentation to mark it as no longer used by production tool files and add a warning against using it with .refine() on tool schemas. (2) constraints.md — rewrote Constraint 57 to flip its rule: the old text mandated .refine() on every dual-path tool schema (now actively wrong), the new text prohibits .refine() on the outer z.object() and documents the correct pattern (plain ZodObject + resolveProjectPath() runtime guard), including an anti-pattern/correct-pattern code block and updated rationale explaining the ZodEffects/MCP SDK incompatibility.

comments.note: WP-004 (Update constraints documentation, assigned to Developer) has a requirement to add a new constraint prohibiting .refine() on tool schemas and an acceptance criterion 'No existing constraints are modified or removed'. With Constraint 57 now corrected by this documentation pass, WP-004 should be re-scoped: the new constraint about ZodEffects/MCP SDK incompatibility can be a forward-looking addition (e.g., a new §60 covering the general rule for all future tools), while Constraint 57 is now current. WP-004 should NOT revert Constraint 57 to its old form.
